subject: SLO alignment + routing questions for Kestrel Health
messages:
From: Ari Cohen <ari.cohen@kestrelhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jaya Rao <jaya.rao@kestrelhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: perf targets and geo routing (Kestrel)

Marcus / team — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick follow-up items from our side so we can finalize the SOW and routing plan: 

- Latency targets: we want to be explicit about P50/P95 for sync inference across regions (US east/west, EU). Internal SLA ask is P50 <= 40ms and P95 <= 120ms for typical 256-token prompts. Can Redwood meet that with hosted variants or do we need Dedicated?
- Throughput/concurrency: our peak is ~1,200 QPS aggregated with traffic split 70% US, 25% EU, 5% APAC. Concurrent sessions (streaming chat) can spike to ~480 concurrent streams; total token generation rate ~2.5M tokens/min at peak.
- Streaming: we require first-token streaming latency < 60ms for US-based users and end-to-end stream stability (no missed tokens) for sessions > 10k tokens.
- Data residency: EU PII must stay in EU datacenters; can routing be enforced per-tenant or per-route, and is KV cache allowed cross-region?

We're attaching a basic SLO matrix and a sketch of our network egress paths. Can you confirm which model variants you'd recommend, whether prefix/KV cache will remain in-region, and whether we should plan for a Dedicated capacity pool for EU traffic?

Thanks — Ari
VP Product, Kestrel Health

Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-topology.png (image)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Cohen <ari.cohen@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: perf targets and geo routing (Kestrel)

Ari — great questions, and thanks for the SLO spreadsheet. High-level answers up front, then a short list of clarifying asks so we can give a firm recommendation: 

High-level:
- Hosted API: for the US traffic with your P50=40ms / P95=120ms targets on 256-token prompts, our verified open-model variants (quantized 4-bit) typically meet p50~25–35ms and p95~90–110ms on our US west GPU fleet at steady concurrency; streaming first-token times are ~30–50ms.
- EU residency: to guarantee data remains in-region for EU PII, we recommend Dedicated or Private in EU; hosted routing can be restricted but we cannot provide tenant-level hard guarantees of never leaving EU without Dedicated/Private.
- Concurrency & throughput: with autoscaling and our continuous batching, 1,200 QPS split as you described is within plausible hosted capacity; however, sustained spikes with 480 concurrent streaming sessions could push cost higher and we usually recommend a Reserved Dedicated pool for predictable p95 during long-running streams.

Clarifying asks (so we can finalize numbers):
1) Can you confirm the 256-token average prompt includes system + user tokens, and whether responses average 128 tokens?
2) Are EU sessions strictly EU-only users, or do you have global users accessing EU-stored conversations?
3) For streaming, do you need per-token ACKs or is client-ordered streaming sufficient?

Next steps we propose: 
- We'll run a short perf qualification run (48 hours) with a small traffic replay from your traces in our US and EU test clusters to produce a measured SLO matrix and recommended instance counts.
- If you want a hard EU residency guarantee, we will scope Dedicated EU nodes; Laura can follow up with capacity/commit pricing.

I'll attach an internal proposal and milestone plan after we confirm the clarifying items. Monica, can you own the perf run coordination once Ari confirms the replay window?

— Marcus
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal-kestrel-v1.pdf (draft)
From: Ari Cohen <ari.cohen@kestrelhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jaya Rao <jaya.rao@kestrelhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: perf targets and geo routing (Kestrel)

Thanks Marcus — answers below: 

1) Yes, 256 tokens is total model context (system + user). Response avg is ~128 tokens.
2) EU sessions are EU residents only; we have a regulatory requirement to keep EU PII in-region. Global users always hit US/EU based on geolocation.
3) Client-ordered streaming is fine; we don't need per-token ACKs, but we need a stable stream with low jitter for UI rendering.

We'll authorize a 48-hour trace share for the perf run. Can you confirm what telemetry you'll need and an approximate blackout window? Also confirm whether KV cache entries for conversation context will be stored in-region.

— Ari
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Cohen <ari.cohen@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: perf targets and geo routing (Kestrel)

Ari — thanks for the quick replies. Next operational items so we can schedule the perf qualification: 

- Telemetry: please provide a 48-hour sampling trace (gzipped ndjson or pcap of API calls) plus a short token distribution CSV. We'll need request timestamps, region geolocation, prompt+response lengths, and a sample of streaming session ids. Redact PII; we only need lengths and timings.
- Blackout window: prefer a Tuesday–Thursday window to avoid weekend variability; can you do Apr 12–13 (UTC)?
- KV cache residency: short answer — KV/prefix cache is colocated with serving nodes. For Hosted we attempt region-local caches but there are edge cases where cache miss routing might cross-region. For strict in-region cache enforcement we will scope Dedicated EU nodes and pin customer KV namespaces to them.
- Deliverables after perf run: measured p50/p95 by region, concurrency envelopes, recommended instance counts, and a recommended routing policy (edge geo-routing + fallback path).

I'll open a HubSpot task and a temporary SFTP link for the trace upload. Laura will follow up on pricing scenarios for Dedicated EU capacity if you want hard residency. Marcus will coordinate the perf run.

Action owners and due dates:
- Ari: confirm Apr 12–13 perf window + upload trace (due Apr 6)
- Marcus: perf-run playbook and test harness (due Apr 9)
- Monica: SFTP + HubSpot task (done by Apr 3)
- Laura: Dedicated EU pricing options (due Apr 8)

If that schedule works we'll issue a short statement of work for the perf qualification and follow with capacity recommendations.

Best — Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
